items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Google AI policy forces decision for San Diego schools – NBC 7 San Diego
items.summary:
As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

“I feel like I see a lot of people using AI now,” said Delilah Ortiz, a student at El Camino High School.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. However, districts that want to continue using Google Search will have to opt in to the AI features.

items.title: Jensen Huang is living proof that AI’s rockstar CEOs are also a hidden risk | CNN Business
items.summary:
Huang has also served as the AI industry’s ambassador on the international stage. He recently met with leaders in European capitals, pitching them on the idea of sovereign AI, where every country needs to build and control its own AI systems.

And Huang has presided over Nvidia’s effort to build out the AI ecosystem. In September, the company disclosed a staggering $99 billion worth of equity investments in this space, up from $2.2 billion two years ago. [...] President Donald Trump, left, and Open AI president Greg Brockman, right, listen as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks at the White House in Washington, DC, on September 29, 2026, after meeting with top executives of AI firms.

When worries about cheaper open models from China sparked selling in global markets, Huang teamed up with Wall Street power players to cobble together a $500 billion plan aimed at keeping the flow of money pumping into AI-powering chips. [...] While Nvidia’s most recent annual financial report to regulators does not directly spell out how much the company’s fate is linked to Huang, the filing does note the company is “highly dependent” on the services of its executive team. It also acknowledges that “failure to ensure effective succession planning” could “hinder our strategic planning, execution and long-term success.”

## AI’s everything man

items.summary:
“That was glaringly obvious during the Salt Typhoon, Colonial Pipeline, and Change Healthcare hacks that affected millions of Americans, and it is an even more urgent problem today as AI tools will accelerate the speed and scale with which bad actors can disrupt our lives and our national security,” Warner said in a statement. “That is why cyber will remain a priority for me as we enter the new Congress and it is why I believe it is critically important we provide our government and the private [...] “I wouldn’t chalk that up solely to the outcome of the election,” Ugoretz told Federal News Network. “There is that, plus just the nature of the world that we’re living in now with some of long-standing challenges with cybersecurity that we faced over the years being accelerated and exacerbated by some of the new AI capabilities, but with a lot of promise too in terms of how AI can help be part of the solution.” [...] “Finally, we will make sure CISA is well-positioned to support the secure development and deployment of AI,” Thompson said.

items.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world | OpenAI
items.summary: Today, we’re sharing advances in how OpenAI models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products. These capabilities span mechanical and electrical engineering and end-to-end system design, and are already helping our internal teams test ideas and iterate faster. [...] of the ability of AI models to positively impact iteration speed for professional workflows. [...] We’re expanding our collaboration with Chip Ganassi Racing (CGR) to explore how OpenAI models can accelerate engineering and prototyping. Working with its R&D team, we’re testing workflows that turn 3D scans of existing parts into editable CAD models and 2D manufacturing drawings. This is particularly useful when the original design files are unavailable.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. [...] protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared. [...] Create opportunities for local workers and businesses.We’ll publish the jobs we expect to create, work with unions and training providers to help residents prepare for them, and report annually on hiring and apprenticeships. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.
